potential_errors: In Worked Witness 2 (C16, p. 2), the 4x4 skew-symmetric matrix J is not defined; under standard choices such as diag(J_2, J_2) or [[0, I_2], [-I_2, 0]], columns (e_1, e_2, e_2, -e_1) yield R J R^T = 2(e_1 e_2^T - e_2 e_1^T) != 0 and HJH != 0, whereas the displayed cancellation e_1 e_2^T - e_2 e_1^T + e_2 e_1^T - e_1 e_2^T = 0 requires either J = diag(J_2, -J_2) or fourth column +e_1.

Table 2 entry C11 reports c_3 = 42 without specifying the input polynomial/tensor instance in the PDF.

summary: This 4-page companion verification preprint provides an independent finite-algebraic audit of Chen Xiangle's deterministic real matrix-product verification paper (arXiv:2611.34814v1), combining 18 Lean 4.35.0 lemmas (reported axiom-clean without Mathlib), a zero-float exact rational and dual-ring Python verifier across 16 certificates, and a constructive clarification of Section 6's dense-quadratic block inequality. All 18 Lean statements in Table 1, the Section 6 aspect-ratio proof, and the worked witnesses (except for an unstated matrix J convention in C16) are algebraically sound, though several Lean theorems formalize elementary arithmetic proxies rather than full general-dimension theorems and external code cannot be executed from the PDF alone.
weaknesses: Several of the 18 Lean theorems presented as 'core algebraic pillars' (Table 1) are elementary arithmetic identities or fixed-dimension proxies—specifically Thm 12 (2*(5*(3s)) = 30s), Thm 14 (r^k <= (kD+1)r^k rather than Lagrange interpolation), Thm 16 (2(n-1) = 2n-2 rather than univariate PIT), and Thm 18 (2-variable integer sum-of-squares rather than general-dimension ker(R^T R) = ker R over R).

Because the Lean files, Python verifier, and test suite reside in an external repository not embedded in the PDF, the claimed 0-sorry build, #print axioms audit, and 29 pytest checks cannot be independently verified from the manuscript alone.

Worked Witness 2 (C16) omits the explicit definition of the skew-symmetric matrix J, leaving the claimed RJR^T = 0 and HJH = 0 cancellation under-specified and false under the standard block-symplectic convention diag(J_2, J_2).
